questions.q: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of an entrepreneur?
options: Being resilient
Being a risk-taker
Being legally responsible
Being environmentally proactive
questions.explanation: An entrepreneur is defined by a willingness to take risks — investing time, resources and finance into an uncertain venture in pursuit of a return. Resilience and legal/environmental responsibility may support entrepreneurship but are not its defining feature.

questions.q: Which of the following is most important to the success of a product?
options: Meeting user needs
Life-time warranty
Built in obsolescence
Conforming to international standards
questions.explanation: A product succeeds first and foremost when it meets the needs of its users; if it does not satisfy a genuine need it will not be adopted. Warranties, obsolescence and standards are supporting factors, not the prime determinant of success.

questions.q: A life cycle analysis of a product is conducted to determine
options: how materials will be manufactured.
the cost of distribution and transport.
the impact of the product on society and the environment.
how materials will be disposed of or recycled.
questions.explanation: A life cycle analysis traces a product from raw material extraction through manufacture, use and disposal to assess its total impact on society and the environment. Manufacturing, transport and disposal are individual stages examined within that broader analysis.

questions.q: A client’s brief to a designer mainly outlines
options: a key design feature.
a summary of all constraints to be considered in the design.
a list of important social and environmental considerations.
a list of consumer demands, legal requirements and budget targets.
questions.explanation: A brief sets out the parameters within which the designer must work — that is, a summary of all the constraints to be considered. The other options describe only individual elements that may sit inside those constraints.

questions.q: Which work health and safety (WHS) consideration should be taken into account during the manufacturing stage of a product?
options: A survey of past employee injuries
Periodic maintenance of machinery and tools
Identification, assessment and control of risks and hazards
Assessment of risks and hazards identified in the use of the final product
questions.explanation: WHS during manufacture follows the risk-management cycle: identifying, assessing and then controlling hazards in the workplace. Injury surveys, machine maintenance and end-use risks are narrower concerns within or beyond that process.

questions.q: Why is it important for designers to protect their intellectual property?
options: It allows competing designers to share ideas.
It enables their ideas to be marketed locally and internationally.
It ensures that all future designs are successfully patented.
It ensures that designer’s ideas cannot be marketed and sold by other designers.
questions.explanation: Protecting intellectual property secures legal ownership so that others cannot market or profit from the designer's ideas without permission. It does not enable sharing, guarantee future patents, or by itself enable marketing.

questions.q: What is the main reason for developing a working prototype?
options: To evaluate operational and functional aspects of the product
To produce a model suitable for advertising on social media
To assist companies in developing a sustainable manufacturing process
To determine aesthetic requirements necessary for production of the product
questions.explanation: A working prototype is built so the designer can test and evaluate how the product operates and functions before committing to production. Advertising, manufacturing process and aesthetics are secondary outcomes, not the main purpose.

questions.q: Which of the following contributes to environmental sustainability?
options: The acceptance of technology and its ease of use
The use of low-cost energy during the manufacturing process
The degradation of physical resources through manufacturing activities
The use of materials and processes without having a significant impact on their surroundings
questions.explanation: Environmental sustainability means using materials and processes that minimise impact on the surrounding environment, preserving resources for the future. Low-cost energy and resource degradation work against sustainability, and ease of use is unrelated.

questions.q: Which of the following is most important in determining the effectiveness of a design?
options: The values and beliefs of the designer
The level of skill and resources available
The design meeting the required end-use
The use of integrated elements and principles of design
questions.explanation: A design is judged effective principally by how well it fulfils its intended end-use or function. The designer's values, available skills, and use of design elements all contribute but are subordinate to fitness for purpose.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a designer with an ethical approach to designing a product?
options: Designing products that meet a niche market
Creating products that avoid excessive resource consumption
Developing marketing campaigns to ensure the greatest number of sales
Examining procedures that protect design ideas and promote creativity
questions.explanation: An ethical approach minimises harm to society and the environment, for example by avoiding excessive consumption of resources. Targeting niche markets, maximising sales and protecting ideas are commercial or legal concerns rather than ethical ones.

questions.topic: Design features and factors affecting design
questions.q:
The images show two different designs of tap turners that have been developed (Figure 1 and Figure 2).

Identify and describe ONE similar and ONE different design feature of the two tap turners shown.

criteria.descriptor: Identifies and shows the characteristics and features of one similar and one different design feature of the tap turners
Identifies one similar AND one different design feature of the tap turners AND sketches in general terms the features of both
Identifies one similar AND one different design feature of the tap turners OR identifies and outlines either one similar OR one different design feature of the tap turners
Identifies one similar OR one different design feature of the tap turners

questions.modelAnswer: A similar feature in both designs is the long handle length, which gives users enough space to grip securely with one or two hands and provides an ergonomic benefit by reducing the strength needed to rotate the tap between ON and OFF. A differing feature is the size and shape of the tap-gripping section: the two designs grip differently sized taps and mould around the tap handle differently, which changes how much pressure the user's hand must apply.

questions.q: Discuss how entrepreneurial activity can influence the success of a product like a tap turner.

criteria.descriptor: Identifies issues and provides points for AND/OR against how entrepreneurial activity can influence the success of a product
Provides characteristics and features of entrepreneurial activity that can influence the success of a product
Sketches in general terms and/or indicates the main features of entrepreneurial activity that can influence the success of a product
Recognises AND/OR names an aspect of entrepreneurial activity that may influence the success of a product

questions.modelAnswer: Entrepreneurial activity can drive a product's success by supplying resources — time, business skills and economic backing — that enable effective market research, manufacturing and promotion. An entrepreneur's networks can promote a tap turner to appropriate niche markets such as senior-citizen organisations, occupational therapists and medical groups, while legal support (trademarks, patents, standards compliance) protects and strengthens the design. Conversely, entrepreneurial activity can also lead to failure if the resources or skills provided result in ineffective manufacturing processes or inappropriate materials that produce a product with minimal function. Overall the entrepreneur's enthusiasm, risk-taking and resource support are vital from the designer's vision through to the final market release.

questions.q: Explain why new and emerging technologies will continue to be developed.

criteria.descriptor: Shows a thorough understanding of why new and emerging technologies will continue to be developed AND makes clear the relationship between the continual development of these technologies and the needs and wants of society and their capacity to facilitate change
Shows a sound understanding of why new and emerging technologies will continue to be developed
Shows some understanding of why new and emerging technologies will continue to be developed
Makes reference to new or emerging technologies

questions.modelAnswer: Society is by nature demanding in its wants and needs for change, so technological change is constant and new technologies will keep being developed to meet that expectation. The ready availability of and access to information shortens the timeframe in which change occurs, while the constant capacity to experiment, the speed of implementation and the ability to produce newly developed products all drive these technologies to evolve. For example, biometric technology began with fingerprint recognition and facial scanning for security, but technological capacity and societal need have since extended it into applications such as detecting and warning of driver fatigue in passenger cars.

questions.q:
In developing innovative and creative designs, designers receive inspiration from a variety of sources.

Explain how these sources influence the designers.

criteria.descriptor: Makes clear the relationship between a variety of sources of inspiration and the development of innovative and creative designs
Shows a sound understanding of how designers are inspired to develop innovative and creative designs
Shows some understanding of how designers are inspired to develop innovative and creative designs
Makes reference to an aspect of inspiration and/or innovative and creative design

questions.modelAnswer: A designer's ability to create innovative and creative designs draws on diverse sources — client and consumer needs, creative thinking, sources of inspiration such as nature, history and culture, evaluation and feedback, and emerging technologies, materials and processes. Stated client or target-market needs provide the criteria for a design that differs from what is currently available, while exploration of existing products, new materials and professional learning extends the designer's skills and knowledge. Continual evaluation and feedback supply fresh ideas that are used to modify existing designs or seed new ones. For example, mobile phones evolved from simple calling devices into multifunction tools because designers sourced and embedded emerging technologies, creating products consumers had not yet seen and generating excitement in society.

questions.q: Analyse how economic, historical and timing factors determine the success or failure of designs.

criteria.descriptor: Draws out and relates implications of how economic, historical and timing factors affect the success or failure of designs
Provides reasons through the use of cause and effect as to how economic, historical and timing factors affect the success or failure of designs
Identifies issues and provides evidence of how economic, historical and timing factors affect the success or failure of designs
Provides characteristics and features of how at least TWO of these factors (economic, historical and timing) affect the success or failure of designs
Sketches in general terms how economic and/or historical and/or timing factors affect the success and/or failure of designs
Identifies a feature of economic or historical or timing factors that affects the success and/or failure of designs

questions.modelAnswer: Economic, historical and timing factors all strongly determine whether a design succeeds or fails. Economically, a product released during a negative climate of high interest rates and low disposable income is less likely to be embraced, so designers must time release to a positive climate or to when the product is most needed — for example launching a Dyson air fan in the warmer spring and summer season, when consumers prioritise cooling even in tough economic times, rather than in winter at a high price. Governments may also provide incentives, financial support and favourable trade conditions in poor periods, improving the economic viability of design and production. Yet some designs succeed regardless of high purchase and upgrade costs: Apple phones and music devices dominate the market because effective marketing makes them perceived as needed and essential, showing that perceived need and timing of release can outweigh pure economic viability. Together these economic, historical and timing factors determine not only sales to the target market but also the broader acceptance and desirability of a design in society.
